item.title: Liverpool is Arsenal’s main rival for World Cup teenage sensation
item.description: Liverpool is Arsenal’s main rival for World Cup teenage sensation Gilberto Mora has attracted Arsenal’s attention after impressing for Mexico at the 2026 World Cup , where he was the youngest player in the competition. Despite his age, the teenager produced some encouraging performances and stood out among the players representing his country. Mora has been regarded as one of the finest young talents in world football for some time, which helped him earn a place in the Mexico squad and receive playing opportunities during the tournament. His performances have further increased interest in his future, with several clubs reportedly monitoring his development . The youngster currently plays for Tijuana, but the Mexican club may struggle to keep hold of him if interest from major European teams continues to grow. Arsenal are among those keen to secure his signature as they look to add another promising young player to their squad. Arsenal step up interest in Mexican youngster The Gunners reportedly view Mora as one of the most exciting young players they could sign and are not keen to wait until the summer before making their move. They are considering an approach in the January transfer window as they look to get ahead of their competitors. However, Arsenal are not alone in the Premier League race for the teenager. According to Sport Witness , Liverpool are also interested in signing him and could compete with the Gunners for his services. The Reds have reportedly followed Mora for some time and have maintained their interest in bringing him to England. They are also considering making an approach in January, meaning Arsenal could face competition from another major Premier League club. (Photo by Azael Rodriguez/Getty Images) Mora faces decision over his next move With both clubs reportedly interested, Mora could have an important decision to make about the next stage of his career. A move to the Premier League would represent a significant opportunity, but he will need to consider which destination offers the right environment for his development. Arsenal will hope their interest and plans to move early can help them secure an agreement, while Liverpool will also be keen to make their long-standing admiration count. For now, Mora remains a Tijuana player, but the growing attention surrounding him could make the January transfer window an important period for his future. item.description: Manchester City's owners have been sent a warning by football regulator David Kogan -Credit:Tom Jenkins, Getty Images Football regulator David Kogan insists he "has the stomach" to take on Manchester City's owners. City are contesting the ruling that they violated more than 100 Premier League financial regulations, and should that appeal fail, they are likely to face further scrutiny from the newly established Independent Football Regulator. The regulator holds the authority to strip City's ownership hierarchy of control, and Kogan assured MPs on the Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee that he will remain immune to any political interference. Florian Wirtz on Liverpool struggles after record transfer and impact of Jürgen Klopp Alejandro Garnacho casts doubt over Aston Villa future after taking drastic action City fans continue to support the board -Credit:Offside via Getty Images Kogan said, via The Mirror : "If you look at the specific sanctions we can impose, we have everything from deciding there is not sufficient evidence to take any action or removing them as directors and from any involvement with the club or English football going forward. But let's be blunt. The two things I was asked about were: would we be subject to political pressure and did we have the stomach to take action? "The answers are: We won't be. And we have the stomach for that. We can't be an independent football regulator and ignore our duties because the club is of a certain size. "Would I, given my choice with an organization that has a relatively new, fairly young staff that's been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don't act, assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?" Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously stated he would be "really concerned" if the fallout led to Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Mansour walking away from the club, with fears also raised that the situation could impact UK trade agreements with the United Arab Emirates. Kogan, however, was emphatic: "We will have to act appropriately. And that is the only test, not the politics around it, not the place where it came from, not the size of the club. It is the only test because without that, you cannot have an effective regulator." item.title: Baylor zeroes in on Jeff Traylor as next football coach. Why a deal could move quickly
item.description: Once it fired Dave Aranda , Baylor conducted a nationwide search for its next football coach. Turns out, the Bears have zeroed in their search some 200 miles from their Waco, Texas, campus — in San Antonio. Nine people with direct knowledge of Baylor’s search process, from college coaches to NFL assistants and industry agents, told USA TODAY Sports in recent days that Baylor has dialed in its search on Texas-San Antonio coach Jeff Traylor. The people requested anonymity due to the sensitivity of the situation. No deal has been finalized but those individuals stressed that, barring unforeseen circumstances, it was expected that Baylor would seek to move forward with Traylor before week’s end. Texas-San Antonio hosts Tulsa on Friday, Nov. 27. The Roadrunners are in first place in the American Conference and would clinch a berth in the title game with a win. They could still reach the game with a loss. The Baylor search party wanted to focus the process on candidates with deep Lone Star State roots, and Taylor’s credentials are hard to match. A Gilbert, Texas, native who played his college football Stephen F. Austin, Traylor merely has spent all but two years of his coaching career since 1989 inside the Texas border. Baylor talked to a bevy of candidates, including top coordinators and sitting head coaches, including UNLV’s Dan Mullen, per people with direct knowledge of the search, but always targeted a candidate with Texas ties. Former Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Robert Griffin III also was part of the search; three different people told USA TODAY Sports that RG3 pushed hard for an opportunity to coach at his alma mater. In addition to his three Texas high school state championships at Gilmer High School, Traylor coached in an assistant role at both the University of Texas and SMU before he logged two years at Arkansas. For the fourth time in seven seasons, Traylor has won nine or more games – and he’s never closed his time atop the Roadrunners with a losing record. In addition to three consecutive bowl wins, Traylor has amassed an overall mark of 60-28 to include an 23-5 mark in the 2022-23 seasons. Traylor, per terms of his contract obtained. USA TODAY Sports, would owe the school $4 million if he exits for another FBS job before Dec. 31, 2026. item.title: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win
item.description: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win As Stuttgart looked to get back to winning ways in Europe following the defeat to Galatasaray, they could hardly have gotten off to a more encouraging start, with the visitors testing Italian giants Inter in the early stages. Maximilian Mittelstädt fired in a teasing ball after six minutes, flying a matter of centimetres past the foot of Ermedin Demirovic. The Bosnian forward, and skipper on the night, would be presented with an opportunity again just over a minute later, linking up well with Chris Führich before seeing a shot blocked. Führich, who was Stuttgart's best player in Istanbul before the international break, remained at the heart of proceedings, seeing an effort well saved by Josep Martinez on the half-volley, before Djed Spence was denied by Dennis Seimen at the other end following the resulting corner. And after the strong Stuttgart start, it would be all Inter for the rest of the half, with Marcus Thuram and Nicolo Barella having the best chances - the former hitting the side netting after a poor Finn Jeltsch backpass, while Barella struck the post with a lovely outside-of-the-boot effort inside the box. Tailing off after the positive start, Stuttgart were looking to avoid the sloppiness that plagued the half outside of the opening 15 minutes. However, after the opening minutes matched the theme of the first half, Inter would be presented with a huge chance to open the scoring, when Federico Dimarco's cross struck the hand of Josha Vagnoman, resulting in a penalty for the hosts after a VAR check. And with a hop and a skip, Petar Sucic would wrong-foot Seimen, sending the ball straight down the middle and giving the Nerazzurri the lead on home soil. Reacting well, Nikolas Nartey would see an effort somehow saved off the line from a corner, while the visitors began to finally regain some of their attacking impetus. Führich and Vagnoman were withdrawn, replaced by Deniz Undav and Jamie Leweling, while Angelo Stiller and Luca Jaquez followed, But just as they were beginning to threaten, with wing-back Mittelstädt calling for a penalty at one end, Inter went up the other end and doubled their lead through the ever-talismanic Lautaro Martinez, who hammered home off the post, catching a bouncing ball ever so sweetly to net his third goal in three Champions League outings. Sebastian Hoeneß cannot argue that the three points deservedly stay in Milan, but once again, he will have to deal with the frustrating topic of his side once again being wasteful. As a result, Stuttgart sit 17th in the standings, with a strong run to the end of the league phase in need, starting with the visit of Lille in two weeks time.

item.title: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting
item.description: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting Manchester United were held to a 2-2 draw by Sporting at the Estádio José Alvalade on Wednesday, 25 November, in the Champions League. A Bruno Fernandes brace was cancelled out by two goals from Luis Suárez in an entertaining game that earned Mauricio Pochettino his first points since taking charge at Old Trafford. The Argentine made four changes to the team that was thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend in the Premier League. Matheus Cunha missed the game due to suspension, while Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt and Patrick Dorgu all dropped to the bench. Harry Maguire and Noussair Mazraoui came into the team, starting at the back alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martínez. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans retained their place in the starting XI, continuing their partnership in midfield. Bruno Fernandes continued in the No. 10 position, with Bryan Mbeumo moving to the left forward role and Amad starting on the right. Joshua Zirkzee started for the first time this season, operating in the No. 9 role. United secure hard-fought draw United had a bright start, but Sporting gradually got a grip on the game. Martínez conceded a penalty, which was saved by Senne Lammens in the 30th minute. However, the Belgian conceded a penalty moments later, which was successfully converted by Luis Suárez in the 33rd minute. The visitors pushed for an equaliser late in the second half, but went into the break trailing 1-0. Martínez made amends early in the second half, winning a penalty which Fernandes converted in the 48th minute. The United skipper then scored a second two minutes later, giving his team the lead. Sporting pushed for an equaliser and finally found one through Suárez in the 80th minute following a Lammens error. United did have the ball in the back of the net late in the game but it was ruled out by VAR. The game ended 2-2, despite the best efforts of Fernandes, who sizzled on his return to his former hunting ground. Page 1 of 5 1 2 3 4 5 Fernandes decisive on Sporting return Bruno Fernandes played the entire 90 minutes on his return to the Estádio José Alvalade, before being replaced in the second half injury time, managing 49 touches of the ball. The Portuguese maestro attempted 44 passes with an 84% accuracy rate. The 32-year-old attempted two crosses and one long ball, but none of them found a teammate. Surprisingly, Fernandes did not register a single key pass in the game. The Portuguese attempted two tackles and was dribbled past once in the game. Fernandes won three of his six duels but lost the ball 13 times. However, it was in the final third where Fernandes crucially made his presence felt. The United skipper registered two shots on target, both of which ended up in the back of the net. He also registered another shot off target, a free-kick that narrowly missed the far post.

item.title: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern
item.description: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern On a night in which Bayern Munich were looking to reset the mood after a week of injuries and controversy behind the scenes, Vincent Kompany would be left to field a far-from-ideal lineup with multiple stars watching on from the sidelines. Konrad Laimer's versatility has been well-documented throughout his years in the Bundesliga, but few could have predicted that the Austrian would be the man to start up top in Lille. And much to their credit, the German record champions did not have to get out of second gear in the first half, despite the rather makeshift lineup. Dayot Upamecano would open the scoring in Northern France after just 15 minutes, rising highest to meet Tom Bischof's corner to head home from six yards out. From then on, Bayern were cruising, before the half-time break completely turned the tide. Lille would see an equaliser disallowed after just a minute of second-half football, when Ayase Ueda bundled over Joshua Kimmich in the build-up to the latter scoring an own goal. But the Mastiffs remained well in the occasion before Ueda netted an equaliser in the 60th minute, and it is hard to say it wasn't deserved after a much better start to the second period. And within a matter of moments, the hosts would take the lead when Ethan Mbappe raced through on goal just to find the post, before Aleksandar Pavlovic bundled the ball into his own net following an attempt to control the ball he will not want to see again. Out of nowhere, Lille had a huge upset win in their sights, while Bayern turned to Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala from the bench, and campus graduates Tim Binder and Noah Codjo-Evore made their European debuts. Soriba Diaoune missed a huge chance to add a third on the volley five minutes out from time, ensuring that the final moments were going to remain uncomfortable for the hosts. But, as much as the makeshift Bayern frontline threw at Lille in the closing stages, the French side were able to hold on for what is a huge win - their first of the Champions League season. Bayern, on the other hand, tasted defeat for the first time in all competitions this term, seeing the rather strange week continue for the record champions.

item.description: The Lakers are on a quest to become a championship-level team . And if history can be an indicator, their hot start to the 2026-27 NBA season suggests they’re on the right path. Lakers star guards Luka Doncic (77) and Austin Reaves (15). NBAE via Getty Images With Monday’s home win over the Jazz , the Lakers improved to 15-3 on the season, which was not only tied with the Spurs for the league’s best record, but also a positive sign for the Lakers’ hopes of being title contenders. This season is the sixth time this century the Lakers have started a season by winning at least 15 of their first 18 games. All five of those seasons ended with the Lakers making the NBA Finals, including winning the title in four of them. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick watches his players. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong The other five times since 2000 that the Lakers won at least 83 percent of their first 18 games were: 2001-2002 (16-2), 2003-04 (15-3), 2008-09 (16-2), 2009-10 (15-3) and 2019-20 (16-2). They won the 2002, ‘09, ‘10 and ‘20 championships after their hot start to those seasons. They made it to the Finals in 2004, which was their fourth championship series appearance in five years, before losing to the Pistons in five games. Walker Kessler, left, and Luka Doncic high-five during a game. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers have won at least 15 of their first 18 games 13 times in franchise history. Half (six of 13) of those seasons ended with them winning the NBA title, while three more ended with them at least making it to the NBA Finals. Another commonality between those seasons is that the Lakers won at least 54 regular season games (or the equivalent of it in an 82-game season in the case of the pandemic-shortened 2019-20) each time they had such a hot start to the season. For a team that was projected to be a borderline playoff contender, that’s great company to be in — a high standard to live up to — but also a sign they’re on the right path.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
